definitions.gloss: original intention; initial resolve; first aspiration
definitions.explanation: The intention or determination one had at the very beginning of an endeavor. Often used when discussing whether someone has stayed true to their original goals.

examples.japanese: {初志|しょし}{貫徹|かんてつ}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to follow through on your original intentions.

examples.japanese: {困難|こんなん}があっても{初志|しょし}を{忘|わす}れてはいけない。
examples.english: Even when facing difficulties, you must not forget your original resolve.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{初志|しょし}を{貫|つらぬ}いて、{十年|じゅうねん}かけて{夢|ゆめ}を{実現|じつげん}した。
examples.english: He stayed true to his original resolve and achieved his dream over ten years.

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the four-character idiom {初志|しょし}{貫徹|かんてつ} (carrying through one's original intention). Outside this set phrase, {初志|しょし} is used on its own to refer to one's initial aspirations or determination.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初志|しょし}{貫徹|かんてつ}: carrying through one's original intention (set phrase)
- {初志|しょし}を{貫|つらぬ}く: to stick to one's original intention
- {初志|しょし}を{忘|わす}れない: to not forget one's original resolve
- {初志|しょし}を{曲|ま}げる: to abandon one's original intention

ETYMOLOGY:
{初|しょ} (first, initial) + {志|し} (will, intention, aspiration).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {初心|しょしん}: beginner's mind, original spirit — broader; also used for 'beginner' ({初心者|しょしんしゃ}) and the phrase {初心|しょしん}に{帰|かえ}る (to go back to basics)
- {志|こころざし}: aspiration, ambition — more general; not limited to one's initial intention
